content.text: gadak has watches and Jira has watchers, and they are unrelated.

local.watches is a personal feed star, kept in local.db and covered by the deliberate exception to the no-original-data rule (specs/000-product/data-model.md:406-422, internal/store/local.go:110-113). `gadak export` exports those. Jira watchers are the site's notification subscribers; they are not mirrored at all, and the skill's escape-hatch example `gadak api GET /rest/api/3/issue/KEY/watchers` is the only way to see them.
So "add Dana as a watcher so she gets notified" can be read as a local star toggle, and an exported watch list can be read as a set of site subscribers. Neither reading is corrected anywhere.

Fix shape: documentation only — separate the two words wherever both appear (skill, data-model, export help), and say plainly that gadak's watch verb is local and does not touch Jira. Mirroring real Jira watchers is deliberately not proposed: mentions and assignment already cover the "make sure this person hears about it" need, and a watcher table would be a large read gap for little agent value.
Found by the Jira-surface gap sweep (track B, score 6/10 — the docs half is cheap, the mirror half is dismissed).
